points.title: 出身与觉醒
points.description: 1928年6月14日出生于罗萨里奥，在布宜诺斯艾利斯完成大学学业。出身中产阶级家庭，父亲是西班牙内战中共和派的支持者，家中藏书丰富，从小受左翼思想熏陶。1950年独自骑自行车游历阿根廷北部乡村。1951-1952年，与友人阿尔贝托·格拉纳多骑摩托车进行长达九个月、穿越八千公里的南美之旅，途经智利、秘鲁、哥伦比亚、委内瑞拉等国。在智利铜矿目睹矿工惨状，在秘鲁麻风病村体会到"最孤立绝望之人之间的最高形式的人类团结"。他在旅行日记中写道：他看到了"因缺钱而无法治疗一个孩子"的无能为力，以及"持续饥饿与惩罚引发的麻木"。这次旅行彻底改变了他——他得出结论：要真正帮助穷人，不能靠医学，而必须进行革命。
points.descriptionEn: Born on June 14, 1928 in Rosario, completed university studies in Buenos Aires. Born into a middle-class family, his father was a supporter of the Republican side in the Spanish Civil War, and the family's rich library exposed him to left-wing thought from an early age. In 1951-1952, he and his friend Alberto Granado embarked on a nine-month, 8,000-kilometer motorcycle journey across South America. Witnessing the plight of miners in Chile and leprosy patients in Peru profoundly changed him. He concluded that to truly help the poor, one must not practice medicine but make revolution.

points.title: 政治激化的熔炉
points.description: 1953年7月抵达危地马拉，时值哈科沃·阿本斯总统推行左翼改革和土地改革，触动美国联合果品公司利益。1954年，美国CIA策动政变推翻阿本斯。年仅26岁的格瓦拉亲历全过程，试图组织抵抗但失败。他后来总结："我当时在危地马拉。然后侵略来了，联合果品公司、美国国务院、杜勒斯发动的侵略……那时我领悟到一个根本的东西：要成为革命医生或革命者，首先必须进行革命。"这一事件让他确信美国绝不会容忍任何拉美左翼政府，武装革命是唯一出路。这是他从"医生"彻底转变为"革命者"的精神转折点。
points.descriptionEn: Arrived in Guatemala in July 1953 during President Jacobo Árbenz's left-wing reforms and land redistribution. In 1954, a CIA-backed coup overthrew Árbenz. The 26-year-old Guevara witnessed the entire process and attempted to organize resistance but failed. This experience convinced him that the United States would never tolerate any left-wing Latin American government, and that armed revolution was the only path forward. This was the spiritual turning point from 'doctor' to 'revolutionary'.

points.title: 命运的汇合
points.description: 1954年9月抵达墨西哥城。在墨西哥城与菲德尔·卡斯特罗和劳尔·卡斯特罗相遇。1955年7月的一个夜晚，他与卡斯特罗彻夜长谈，当即决定加入"七二六运动"。绰号"切"诞生于此——阿根廷人常用感叹词"che"（相当于"嗨"），墨西哥战友以此称呼他。接受严格军事训练后，1956年11月25日，82名革命者挤在破旧的"格拉玛号"游艇上出发。若没有这次相遇，他可能只是阿根廷众多左翼知识分子之一。这里是他人生的决定性拐点。
points.descriptionEn: Arrived in Mexico City in September 1954. Met Fidel and Raúl Castro there. On a night in July 1955, after an all-night conversation with Castro, he immediately decided to join the 26th of July Movement. His nickname 'Che' was born here — Argentines commonly use the interjection 'che', and his Mexican comrades called him by it. After rigorous military training, on November 25, 1956, 82 revolutionaries set sail crammed into the dilapidated yacht 'Granma'. Without this encounter, he might have remained just one of Argentina's many left-wing intellectuals.

points.title: 革命与执政
points.description: "格拉玛号"登陆遭遇政府军伏击，幸存者仅二十余人逃入马埃斯特腊山区。格瓦拉凭借军事才能迅速成为卡斯特罗最信任的指挥官之一。1958年12月指挥圣克拉拉战役，夺取一列满载政府军的装甲列车，彻底击溃巴蒂斯塔政府军士气。1959年1月2日率先率部进入哈瓦那。执政期间，任卡瓦尼亚城堡监狱检察长（负责审判巴蒂斯塔政权人员）、国家银行行长（在古巴纸币上签下"Che"）、工业部长。主导土地改革、全国扫盲运动。在猪湾事件中训练民兵击退入侵者，在1962年导弹危机中扮演引入苏联核导弹的关键角色。1963-1965年古巴"大辩论"中，公开批评苏联模式，主张"道德激励"而非"物质激励"建设社会主义。1964年12月在联合国大会发表反帝演讲。古巴是他人生的巅峰——从无名医生成为革命英雄、政府高官、国际名人。
points.descriptionEn: The Granma landing was ambushed by government forces, with only about twenty survivors escaping into the Sierra Maestra mountains. Guevara quickly became one of Castro's most trusted commanders. In December 1958, he commanded the Battle of Santa Clara, capturing an armored train full of government troops and shattering Batista's military morale. On January 2, 1959, he led the first troops into Havana. During governance, he served as prosecutor at La Cabaña Fortress, President of the National Bank (signing Cuban banknotes as 'Che'), and Minister of Industry. He led land reform and the national literacy campaign, trained militia to repel the Bay of Pigs invasion, and played a key role in introducing Soviet nuclear missiles during the 1962 Missile Crisis. Cuba was the peak of his life — from an unknown doctor to revolutionary hero, high-ranking official, and international celebrity.

points.title: 非洲的挫折
points.description: 1965年4月率约100名古巴志愿者秘密支援刚果"辛巴叛乱"武装。行动彻底失败：当地武装缺乏纪律、组织混乱，语言文化隔阂严重，农民不配合。他在日记中沮丧地写道："刚果的农民没有帮助我们……革命领袖们已经丧失了革命热情。"这是他革命生涯中第一次重大军事失败，但未动摇他的信念，反而使他更执着于"游击中心"理论。
points.descriptionEn: In April 1965, he led about 100 Cuban volunteers to secretly support the Simba rebellion in Congo. The operation was a complete failure: local forces lacked discipline, organization was chaotic, language and cultural barriers were severe, and peasants did not cooperate. He wrote dejectedly in his diary about the failure. This was the first major military defeat of his revolutionary career, but it did not shake his convictions — instead, it made him more committed to the foco theory of guerrilla warfare.

points.title: 最后的殉道
points.description: 1966年11月化名"拉蒙"潜入玻利维亚，试图以玻利维亚为基地将革命扩散至整个拉美。行动从一开始即陷入困境：得不到当地农民支持（甚至有农民向政府军举报），美国CIA提供情报和军事顾问，玻利维亚政府军大规模围剿。1967年10月8日在拉伊格拉村附近受伤被俘。次日，在玻利维亚总统授意下被枪决，终年39岁。遗言传为："开枪吧，胆小鬼，你不过是杀一个人罢了。"遗体被秘密埋葬，双手被砍下验证身份。1997年遗骸被找到并运回古巴，安葬于圣克拉拉。肉身终结之地，革命殉道之所。正如卡斯特罗所言："他们以为杀了他就能令他停止战斗……但今天，他无处不在。"
points.descriptionEn: In November 1966, under the alias 'Ramón', he infiltrated Bolivia, attempting to use it as a base to spread revolution across Latin America. The operation was troubled from the start: no support from local peasants (some even reported him to government forces), CIA intelligence and military advisors assisting, and large-scale Bolivian military operations against him. On October 8, 1967, he was wounded and captured near the village of La Higuera. The next day, on orders from the Bolivian president, he was executed at age 39. His reported last words: 'Shoot, coward, you are only going to kill a man.' His remains were found and returned to Cuba in 1997, buried in Santa Clara.

supporter.zh: 对左翼支持者而言，格瓦拉是最纯粹的国际主义革命者——他放弃了阿根廷的出身、古巴的高位和舒适生活，甘愿为全球被压迫者献身。他被视为反帝精神的象征、游击战理论的实践者，以及"新人"理想的倡导者——主张以道德激励而非物质利益推动社会主义建设。核心遗产包括：游击战理论（"游击中心"学说）影响了全球数十个解放运动；独立的反帝立场——不屈从于美国或苏联任何一方；国际主义精神——超越国界的革命视野。曼德拉称他"鼓舞"了一代又一代人。在古巴，至今每天有学生宣誓"我们会像切一样"（Seremos como el Che）。
supporter.en: For left-wing supporters, Guevara is the purest internationalist revolutionary — he gave up his Argentine origins, high position in Cuba, and comfortable life, willingly sacrificing himself for the oppressed of the world. He is seen as a symbol of anti-imperialist spirit, a practitioner of guerrilla warfare theory, and an advocate of the 'New Man' ideal — promoting moral incentives over material benefits in building socialism. His core legacy includes: guerrilla warfare theory (foquismo) that influenced dozens of liberation movements worldwide; an independent anti-imperialist stance — refusing to submit to either the United States or the Soviet Union; and an internationalist spirit — a revolutionary vision transcending national boundaries. Mandela said he 'inspired' generations. In Cuba, students still pledge daily 'We will be like Che' (Seremos como el Che).

critic.zh: 对批评者而言，格瓦拉是危险的乌托邦暴力革命家。主要争议包括：暴力手段——在卡瓦尼亚城堡批准处决数百人，明确宣称"武装斗争是争取自由的唯一途径"；经济唯意志论——在古巴工业部长任内以道德激励取代物质规律，被批评为脱离客观条件；战略破产——刚果和玻利维亚的失败证明，"游击中心"缺乏群众基础的外来武装无法成功；忽视自由与法治——被批评低估了民主制度、公民自由和少数人权利的价值。评论家阿尔瓦罗·巴尔加斯·略萨将其理念视为第三世界苦难的来源，批评其"将法律置于最强者之下"。
critic.en: For critics, Guevara is a dangerous utopian revolutionary. Main controversies include: violence — approving hundreds of executions at La Cabaña fortress, explicitly declaring 'armed struggle is the only way to freedom'; economic voluntarism — replacing material laws with moral incentives during his tenure as Minister of Industry, criticized as detached from objective conditions; strategic bankruptcy — the failures in Congo and Bolivia proved that externally-imposed foco theory without a mass base cannot succeed; disregard for freedom and rule of law — criticized for underestimating the value of democratic institutions, civil liberties, and minority rights. Commentator Álvaro Vargas Llosa views his ideas as a source of suffering in the Third World.

objective.zh: 历史学界将格瓦拉视为矛盾的复合体——既是杰出的游击战术家和不屈的国际主义者，又是固执的唯意志论者和乌托邦空想家。他的反帝思想近年来受到更多重视，被视为全球南方对西方主导秩序的系统性批判。流行文化层面，阿尔贝托·科尔达拍摄的《英勇的游击队员》肖像已成为全球最著名的符号之一。从1968年巴黎学生运动到世界各地的抗议游行，从T恤到海报，他的形象被反复复制，代表着反叛、反资本主义和"年轻叛逆精神"。然而讽刺的是，这种商业化恰恰是他所反对的消费主义。有学者指出，尽管"切"成了一个被掏空内容的符号，"当年引导他走上革命之路的不公与不平等仍然存在"，这正是其形象持久生命力的根源。
objective.en: Historical academia views Guevara as a complex paradox — both an outstanding guerrilla tactician and unyielding internationalist, yet also a stubborn voluntarist and utopian idealist. His anti-imperialist thought has received renewed attention in recent years, seen as a systematic critique of Western-dominated global order from the Global South. In popular culture, Alberto Korda's photograph 'Guerrillero Heroico' has become one of the world's most famous symbols. From the 1968 Paris student movement to protest marches worldwide, from T-shirts to posters, his image has been endlessly reproduced, representing rebellion, anti-capitalism, and 'youthful defiance'. Yet ironically, this commercialization is precisely the consumerism he opposed. Scholars note that although 'Che' has become an emptied symbol, 'the injustices and inequalities that led him onto the revolutionary path still exist' — which is the root of his image's enduring vitality.

self.zh: 无论死亡在何处降临，只要我们的战斗呐喊传到了一个愿意倾听的耳朵，只要有另一只手伸出来接过我们的武器，那它都是受欢迎的。
self.en: Wherever death may surprise us, let it be welcome, provided that this, our battle cry, may have reached some receptive ear and another hand may be extended to wield our weapons.

others.zh: 他们以为杀了他就能令他停止战斗……但今天，他无处不在，只要有正义要维护。
others.en: They thought that by killing him he would cease to fight... but today he is everywhere, wherever there is a just cause to defend.
